Perf(Extractor): Cache hot paths + iterative trim + hoisted regexes

Two-phase optimisation, no public API change. All 30 unit tests pass
(25 baseline + 5 new cache regression tests); pnpm lint clean.

# Phase A — internal caches in CSSExtractor

- **content-hash cache** (`contentHashes`): skip the entire
  extract→validate→insert pipeline when (source, content) is unchanged.
  HMR re-fires on the same file are now near-zero cost.
- **valid-rules memo** (`validRulesCache`): the same class string is
  validated once and reused. In a 1000-file codebase where `bg:white`
  appears in 200 files, this drops from 200 × `generateValidRules` to 1.
- **getter memoisation**: `fixedSourcePaths` and `allowedSourcePaths`
  no longer re-glob the filesystem on every property access. Cleared on
  `reset()`.
- **single-pass filter**: was three sequential `.filter()` chains
  (invalid / valid / excludeClasses), each allocating a new array.
  Replaced with one for-loop that short-circuits on each guard.
- **drop sham `Promise.all(map(async))`**: `generateValidRules` is
  synchronous; the promise wrap was pure microtask overhead with no
  parallelism in single-threaded JS.

# Phase B — extract-latent-classes internals

- **All regex literals hoisted to module scope** so they're parsed once
  at load instead of being re-encountered (V8 already memoises locals,
  but module scope makes the intent explicit).
- **Iterative `trimString`** (was recursive-to-fixpoint): no stack
  growth on long inputs.
- **Merged `needExclude` keep-patterns** into one `KEEP_TOKEN` regex,
  short-circuiting before the explicit reject list — most input fails
  the first check, so we avoid 11 redundant regex evaluations.
- **CSS unit suffix** pulled to a constant; the gigantic `WxH` regex
  no longer inline-duplicates the unit list.
- **Local regex per `peelCompleteString` call** — using a shared
  module-level regex with /g would corrupt outer `lastIndex` during
  recursion (caught while writing this).

# Verification

  fixtures, `<style>` strip, comments, `@font-face`, `~/path`, group
  syntax, content quote, url, wxh)
- 5 new cache.test.ts cases cover content-hash hit/miss/invalidate,
  reset(), and per-class memoisation
- `pnpm lint` clean

Fix(Static): Three races in webpack & vite HMR pipelines

C1 — webpack `compilation.hooks.succeedModule.tap()` ran an `async`
callback whose Promise tapable discarded (succeedModule is a
SyncHook). Webpack proceeded to `emit` while `extractor.insert()`
was still pending, so output CSS could be missing classes from
late-arriving modules.

  Fix: synchronously record source in `succeedModule`, then await
  every pending insert in one `finishModules.tapPromise()`. webpack
  blocks on AsyncSeriesHook promises before processing assets.

C3 — `VirtualCSSHMRPlugin.handleReset` built a `tasks` array then
called `tasks.concat(...)`. `Array#concat` returns a new array
without mutating; every promise from the module-graph re-insertion
arm was silently dropped on the floor. After config-file save, HMR
could publish CSS before reset had finished re-extracting open
modules.

  Fix: `tasks.push(...arr)`. Also drop the inline `await
  prepare()` (which defeated the parallel `Promise.all`) and await
  `updateVirtualModule` so the chain actually settles before the
  next event.

C4 — the `reset` and `change` listeners attached to the extractor
were `() => servers.forEach(s => fn(s))` with no await. EventEmitter
does not await async listeners; two saves arriving in quick
succession would mutate `extractor.css` concurrently.

  Fix: chain reset / update onto Promise queues (one each), so a
  second event is queued behind the first. Errors are caught and
  logged instead of becoming unhandled rejections. As a side-effect
  `updateVirtualModule` now awaits `server.reloadModule()` so the
  serialisation is observable end-to-end.

Fix(Vite): Vite static-extract bugs in placeholder, include, transform

This PR targets the *vite build* path (mode: 'extract') of the static-
generation pipeline. Three latent issues plus one extractor cleanup,
none of which alter the public PluginOptions surface.

D1 — virtual-css-module placeholder leak

  `VirtualCSSModulePlugin.generateBundle` did a literal
  `String.replace()` on every CSS asset to swap the slot placeholder
  (`#virtual\:master\.css{--slot:0}`) for the real extracted CSS, and
  silently no-op'd if the placeholder was not found. Any downstream
  PostCSS plugin or CSS minifier that rewrote / dropped that rule
  (unescaping `\:`, normalising whitespace, eliminating an apparent
  unused selector) made the build ship CSS missing every extracted
  class. The user only found out at runtime against a blank page.

  Fix: track whether the virtual module was ever loaded; in
  `generateBundle`, count how many CSS assets received a successful
  replacement; if the placeholder was emitted but no asset matched
  AND there is real CSS to splice, emit `this.warn(...)` so the
  failure surfaces at build time.

C7 — extract mode silently overrode user `extractor.include`

  `master-css:extractor.configResolved` did
  `context.extractor.options.include = []` unconditionally, wiping a
  user-supplied `extractor: { include: [...] }` option without telling
  them. Now only blanked when the user did NOT pass an explicit array
  — letting them seed extra paths (e.g. `node_modules/some-lib/dist`)
  that Vite's `transform` hook would not otherwise feed.

C8 — extract mode `transform` accepted every non-`.css` module

  Json, png-as-module, `?import` / `?url` query requests, and 3rd-
  party virtual modules all got pumped through the regex-heavy
  `extractLatentClasses` and the rules validator. Now restricted to
  a file-extension allow-list (`html|js|jsx|ts|tsx|svelte|astro|vue
  |md|mdx|pug|php`) mirroring the extractor's default include glob;
  Vite query suffixes (`?import` / `?raw` / `?vue&...`) are honoured.

C6 — dead foundConfigPath / foundOptionsPath in extractor core

  Both `configPath` and `optionsPath` getters assigned a
  `foundConfigPath` local that was never read, then returned the
  basename-only `foundBasename`. Looks like an incomplete refactor.
  Inlined the existsSync check, dropped the dead variable.

Fix(Integration): Load browser manifest via fetch to avoid import attributes (#443)

The browser manifest facades built a loader with
`new Function('specifier', "return import(specifier, { with: { type: 'json' } })")`.
JSON import attributes (`with { type: 'json' }`) are only supported in Safari
17.2+, Chrome 123+ and Firefox 130+. On older engines, notably every iOS 15
and iOS 16 (Safari < 17.2), evaluating that dynamic import, even inside
`new Function`, throws `SyntaxError: import call expects exactly one argument`
while the entry module is evaluated. Because the manifest facade runs at the
top level of the app entry, the whole app fails to bootstrap and renders a
blank page with no obvious console error.

The syntax is invisible to build-time tooling because it lives inside a
`new Function` string, so bundler and esbuild target checks never flag it.

Load the manifest with `fetch().then(r => r.json())` in the browser facades
(`toBrowserManifestFacadeModule` and the browser branch of
`toUniversalManifestFacadeModule`). Fetch is universally supported and needs no
bundler-hiding indirection. The Node facades keep the JSON import attribute,
since Node supports it. Verified on an iOS 15.5 Safari simulator: blank before,
mounts after.
